skill.name: planner
skill.description: Create phased implementation plans with sprints, atomic tasks, validation steps, and follow-up questions for unclear requirements.
skill.summary: Turn unclear implementation requests into structured, testable plans.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: All four static findings appear to be false positives in Markdown instructional content. The backtick detections are inline code or a fenced Markdown plan template, and the documentation-search sentence is not system reconnaissance.

static_findings.snippet: This will narrow and aid you in finding the right docs.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 88 contains inline Markdown showing the literal filename suffix `-plan.md`. It does not invoke a shell, Ruby backticks, or any executable command.
Line 91 is a Markdown example mapping a user request to the filename `xyz-bug-plan.md`. The backticks are formatting only and do not execute code.
Line 103 opens a fenced Markdown block for a plan template. The content is documentation output format, not a command execution primitive.
Line 33 says clarifying requirements will help find the right docs. This is normal planning guidance and does not instruct host reconnaissance or data collection.

content.value_statement: Complex coding work can become unclear when scope, dependencies, and validation steps are missing. This skill creates phased plans with sprints, atomic tasks, and verification checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Investigates codebase structure, patterns, dependencies, and related components before planning.
Prompts for clarifying requirements before documentation lookup or task breakdown.
Uses current official documentation for external libraries, APIs, frameworks, or services when available.
Creates sprint-based plans with demoable increments, atomic tasks, dependencies, and validation steps.
Generates Markdown plan files with request-based kebab-case filenames.
Reviews the saved plan for gotchas, unclear areas, missing steps, and follow-up questions.
limitations: It creates plans only and explicitly does not implement the requested changes.
Plan quality depends on the clarity of the request and user answers.
External documentation lookup depends on the availability of a compatible documentation retrieval tool.
Effort estimates and sprint boundaries are planning aids, not delivery guarantees.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Build
use_cases.description: Break a feature request into phased work, files to change, tests, and demo checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Prepare Bug Fix Work
use_cases.description: Convert an unclear defect report into research steps, acceptance criteria, validation, and rollback planning.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Technical Delivery
use_cases.description: Create a shared implementation plan with dependencies, sequencing, risks, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the planner skill to create a plan for this change: [describe the change]. Include phases, tasks, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: A defect needs investigation before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the planner skill to plan a fix for this bug: [describe symptoms]. Include research steps, likely files, acceptance criteria, and rollback guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature with Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: A feature touches several components or services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the planner skill to plan this feature: [feature description]. Ask clarifying questions, identify dependencies, and split work into demoable sprints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a High-Risk Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with sequencing, risks, and verification needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the planner skill to create a migration plan for [system or framework]. Include documentation checks, parallelizable tasks, test strategy, risks, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Plan the implementation of team invitations for a SaaS app.
output_examples.output: A phased plan with an overview, prerequisites, sprint goals, invite-flow tasks, email and permission checks, test coverage, risks, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: Break down a fix for failed password reset links.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting plan covering reproduction, token validation, mailer checks, route updates, regression tests, user-facing validation, and release verification.

output_examples.input: Create a migration plan from one payment provider to another.
output_examples.output: A migration roadmap with documentation review, data mapping, feature flags, staged rollout, monitoring, rollback criteria, and acceptance checks.

best_practices: Provide goals, constraints, target users, and existing context before asking for a plan.
Answer clarifying questions before requesting the final task breakdown.
Review each sprint for a runnable validation step before implementation starts.
anti_patterns: Using the plan as final implementation without developer review.
Skipping clarifying questions when scope, risks, or dependencies are unclear.
Requesting a large plan without identifying non-goals or rollout constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates implementation plans and explicitly avoids implementing the work.

faq.question: Can it plan work for existing codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to inspect architecture, patterns, dependencies, and related components before drafting tasks.

faq.question: Will it ask follow-up questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks clarifying questions before documentation lookup and may ask more after reviewing plan risks.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. Plans include validation steps, demo checks, and a testing strategy for each sprint.

faq.question: Can it use current library documentation?
faq.answer: Yes, when a compatible documentation retrieval tool is available and the plan involves external dependencies.

faq.question: What file does it create?
faq.answer: It saves a Markdown plan using keywords from the request and a kebab-case plan filename.
